card: Verify Proton Experimental or game-forced version in game Properties > Compatibility. Clear shader cache under ~/.steam/steam/steamapps/shadercache/<appid>.
Try fullscreen vs borderless windowed; some titles hitch only in one mode on Deck.
Check ProtonDB for launch options and community fixes before forcing a Proton version.
After SteamOS update, re-test with Proton Experimental; stale compat data can break until shader regen.
On Windows Steam, Proton is not used; troubleshooting is native DirectX/Vulkan driver issues.
Deck sleep with Proton games: if resume fails, exit to Gaming Mode home and relaunch.
Winetricks/dotnet installs are last resort; prefer official Proton or game-specific fixes.
Force Proton 8.x or Experimental from game Properties when default fails after title update.
If audio crackles under Proton, try gamescope -e or disable RT audio in game settings.
Proton log: PROTON_LOG=1 %command% captures useful launch traces to ~/steam-*.log.
VR under Proton on Deck is limited; prefer native Linux VR builds or host PC streaming.
Verify AC adapter wattage; weak USB-C hubs can throttle charge and TDP during play.
After long sessions, check fan noise and surface temp; pause and lower TDP if throttling.
MicroSD for library: use A2-rated cards; slow SD increases load times.
Desktop Mode vs Gaming Mode: some fixes only apply in Desktop Mode.
Reboot clears stuck GPU/audio states after failed game exit or suspend bugs.
Factory reset is last resort; backup ~/.steam and compatdata paths first.
Steam Deck verified badge is guidance; check ProtonDB for edge cases.
USB-C dock display issues: try direct cable, update dock firmware.
Bluetooth audio latency: prefer wired for rhythm and competitive games.
Battery health: avoid 100% storage for weeks; occasional full cycle helps reporting.
Steam Machine uses SteamOS; same Proton and gamescope paths as Deck.
Big Picture Mode is default on Deck; Desktop Mode for Konsole and file fixes.
Return to Gaming Mode from Desktop via desktop icon or steam command in Konsole.
Desktop Mode file manager can delete shader cache and compatdata when games corrupt.
Gaming Mode QAM is safe for TDP and brightness without leaving the game.
Steam Machine class hardware: verify AMDGPU and Mesa match SteamOS channel.
BPM keyboard: Steam + X opens on-screen keyboard in Gaming Mode.
Switching modes mid-game can lose fullscreen focus; exit game first.
Non-Steam games via Wine/Proton need added as Non-Steam shortcuts with forced Proton.
Wine prefix corruption: delete compatdata folder only after backing up saves.
Heroic/Lutris titles are outside Steam compatdata; paths differ from Steam library.
32-bit Wine deps on Linux: use Proton bottle instead of raw Wine when possible.
Wine does not run on Windows; use native builds or VMs.
DXVK/VKD3D versions ship with Proton; avoid random DLL overrides without logs.
Verify game files integrity from Steam client before driver reinstalls.
Clear download cache: Steam Settings > Downloads > Clear Download Cache.
Launch options apply per game; -dx11 / -dx12 / -fullscreen flags are common.
Steam client beta vs stable: switch channel if social UI breaks after update.
Windows Game Mode and Game Bar can conflict; test with overlays off.
Antivirus scanning Steam library causes stutter; exclude library path cautiously.
SteamVR requires HMD drivers; reboot HMD after GPU driver updates.
Room setup drift: redo standing calibration and check base station angles.
Deck as SteamVR host is not supported; stream from PC or use standalone HMD.
Mirror vs headset-only display: wrong choice can black-screen the desktop.
USB bandwidth: VR headsets need direct motherboard USB3 ports.
OpenXR vs SteamVR runtime toggle per game in Properties or launcher.
Controller binding conflicts: reset to default in SteamVR Input settings.
Wireless VR: Wi-Fi 6 and line-of-sight reduce encode stutter.
Gamescope wraps the game process; resolution and FSR flags apply at launch.
Deck native resolution vs scaled: lower internal res + FSR can stabilize FPS.
gamescope -W/-H set output size; mismatched aspect causes letterboxing.
Nested gamescope in Desktop Mode can fail; prefer Gaming Mode launch.
HDR titles may need experimental SteamOS builds with gamescope.
Frame limiter in gamescope can reduce fan noise when uncapped spikes occur.
If game ignores resolution, set in-game resolution to match gamescope target.
MangoHud + gamescope: wrap game inside gamescope first.
Kernel anti-cheat needs developer Proton enablement; check ProtonDB status.
Easy Anti-Cheat offline modes may work when online blocked on Linux.
On Windows, repair anti-cheat service via game launcher or reinstall.
Secure boot rarely affects Deck; focus on Proton anti-cheat flags.
Faceit/Vanguard class AC: often no Linux support; use Windows PC.
After AC update, verify patch notes for Linux experimental support.
Multiplayer blocked on Deck is often AC policy, not TDP misconfig.
Proton BattlEye runtime: Steam may prompt install once per title.
Remote Play from PC: host encoding load matters; lower host resolution if client stutters.
Remote Play Together uses host PC; Deck as guest needs stable LAN Wi-Fi.
Moonlight/Sunshine: tune bitrate to 20-50 Mbps on local LAN.
Host-side fixes first: GPU encoder driver, HEVC support, firewall.
Deck as client: disable client upscale if bandwidth limited.
Audio chop on stream: try wired LAN or 5 GHz Wi-Fi.
VR streaming doubles encode cost; reduce supersampling on host.
Sleep host PC during stream drops session; wake host before reconnect.
Move library to SD: Steam Settings > Storage; move per game.
compatdata on SD moves with game if selected; shaders may need regen.
Internal storage full: uninstall large shaders and unused games first.
ext4 on SD: SteamOS formats SD; do not reformat to NTFS for library.
Repair library folder permissions if games fail to update after SD remount.
NTFS library on Windows: avoid compressing Steam folder.
Cloud save sync fails when storage full; free space before blaming network.
Backup ~/.steam/steam/userdata before storage migrations.
SteamOS update stuck: reboot and retry; recovery image if boot loop.
Game update mid-download: clear cache and verify files if manifest corrupt.
Windows Update + GPU driver same week: reboot twice before blaming games.
Steam client update can reset per-game Proton choice; re-check Compatibility.
Mesa/AMD driver in SteamOS: system updates ship GPU stack.
Rollback SteamOS only via recovery; not per-game.
Per-game controller config: gear icon in library > Controller Options.
Gyro aim: enable in controller config > Gyro > Always On for shooters.
Desktop layout vs Gamepad layout: wrong template breaks controls.
Steam Input vs native gamepad: force Steam Input on or off explicitly.
Back paddle L4/R4: map in Controller Settings > Edit Layout.
Steam Input on Windows requires Steam client in background.
Multiplayer layouts: check Steam Input community configs.
Keyboard mouse on Deck: Desktop Mode or Touchscreen in layout editor.
Cyberpunk and FPS: community gyro templates need sensitivity tweak.
SteamVR controllers use separate binding UI from flat Steam Input.
Bluetooth pairing: hold Steam + X, use Bluetooth in Gaming Mode.
Wired USB controller preferred for lowest latency.
Calibrate gyro on flat surface before enabling gyro aim.
PS5 DualSense on Deck: works via Bluetooth; adaptive triggers not supported.
Xbox controller firmware updates require Windows PC or mobile app.
Stick drift: increase deadzone in Steam Input or clean hardware.
Gyro jitter when walking: lower sensitivity or disable on foot sections.
Multiple controllers: player order follows connection order.
Check the battery first; a controller that seems broken is often just empty.
If a controller stops responding mid-game, disconnect and reconnect it before restarting the game.
If it connects but no buttons do anything, forget the device and pair it again.
Weak or missing vibration usually means it connected as a generic device, not through Steam Input.
Steam Frame with bonsAI: run bonsAI on a Steam Deck on the same home network. There is no bonsAI inside the headset.
Point bonsAI at the PC that streams your Frame games: the PC address followed by :11434. On that PC, Ollama must accept connections from other devices and port 11434 must pass the firewall.
The PC streaming your game is the best place to run the model. Same machine, no extra hop.
Frame comfort: reduce locomotion intensity; a seated playspace reduces nausea.
VR framerate misses feel worse than flat-screen ones. Prefer a lower refresh rate that holds over a higher one that stutters.
Screenshots taken while streaming save on the host PC, not on the Deck running bonsAI.
If a flat game opens on the wrong display, check the display or output target before changing graphics settings.
FEX-Emu on ARM Linux: experimental x86 emulation; not AMD Deck path.
FEX vs Proton: Proton is primary on Steam Deck AMD.
Steam offline mode: go online once to validate licenses before offline trip.
DNS issues on hotel Wi-Fi: try manual DNS in Desktop Mode network settings.
EmuDeck paths: ROMs and emulator configs live outside Steam.
PCSX2 via EmuDeck: per-game settings in EmuDeck menu.
Flatpak Steam vs native: Deck uses system Steam; do not mix library paths.
Shader pre-cache missing: first launch stutters until cache builds.
On the Deck a crash drops you back to the game library, not to a desktop -- there is no desktop to check.
Disable Steam overlay and third-party overlays when crashes happen at launch.
Try forcing a different Proton version, or Proton Experimental, from the game's Properties > Compatibility tab.
Clear the shader cache under ~/.steam/steam/steamapps/shadercache/<appid> and let it rebuild.
Verify the game's files from the Steam library; a broken download is a common crash cause.
Check free storage space -- a nearly full drive can crash a game at launch or while saving.
Update both the game and SteamOS before digging further; a version mismatch is a frequent cause.
A real kernel panic (not just a game crash) is rare on Deck -- note the SteamOS version and last game if it happens.
If only one game crashes and everything else runs fine, the game is the more likely cause.
TDP cap in QAM affects CPU/GPU together; lowering reduces heat.
30 FPS cap can stabilize frame pacing vs uncapped stutter.
If the game stutters, lower the resolution or turn on FSR before changing anything else.
Cap the frame rate to what the game can hold steady -- a lower steady rate beats an uneven higher one.
Lower the TDP limit in Quick Settings if the Deck feels hot or the fan is loud.
Plug in the charger during demanding games; the Deck slows itself down on low battery.
Turn off motion blur and other post-processing effects; some games run noticeably smoother without them.
Verify the game's files if performance suddenly got worse right after an update.
Give the game a minute after launch -- shaders compiling for the first time cause stutter that goes away.
Close other apps and background downloads before a demanding game to free up memory.
No audio after suspend: toggle volume, switch output in Quick Settings.
Check the output device in Quick Settings -- the Deck can switch to a disconnected Bluetooth device.
Re-pair Bluetooth headphones if the audio crackles or cuts in and out.
Use a wired connection for rhythm or competitive games; Bluetooth audio adds a small delay.
If there is no sound at all, check the in-game audio settings too, not just the Deck's.
Restart the game if sound stops mid-session; it is usually the game's audio, not the hardware.
Try a different USB-C dock or cable if audio through a dock cuts out or hums.
Update the game if audio broke right after a patch; a fix is usually already out.
External monitor blank: try HDMI direct, 1080p60, disable overscan.
If the screen looks torn while moving the camera, turn on V-Sync in the game's display settings.
Set an external display to 1080p60 first -- higher settings can show a blank screen until confirmed working.
Use a direct HDMI cable instead of an adapter chain if an external monitor shows nothing.
Lower the in-game resolution if the picture looks blurry on the built-in screen.
Turn off HDR in the game if colors look washed out or too dark on the built-in screen.
If the picture stutters rather than tears, that is a performance problem, not a display one.
Restart the game after changing display settings; some games only apply them on the next launch.
Launch option moshortcut://"F4SE" (Properties > Launch Options) starts the game through F4SE via Mod Organizer 2. Confirmed on the maintainer's own Deck, 2026-08-21.
Launch option %command% -dx12 (Properties > Launch Options) runs on the maintainer's own Deck. What it fixes is unconfirmed -- a launch option they use, not a documented fix for a specific symptom.
Researched, unconfirmed: the Render Scale slider also blurs menu/HUD text -- no separate UI-scale option. Below ~90% text gets hard to read; raise Render Scale rather than blame the screen.
Researched, unconfirmed: Ship of Harkinian's enhancements menu (framerate, resolution, saves, textures) has no gamepad-only way in -- map a trackpad as a mouse first, or it stays unreachable.
Researched, unconfirmed: gyro in Ship of Harkinian reads as a joystick axis, not mouse-look. Pick the control scheme matching a joystick-style gyro, or camera gyro won't respond.
